newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM says '97 budget to end costly borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM says '97 budget to end costly borrowing.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Friday Turkey's 1997 draft budget, which envisages a zero deficit, would allow the treasury to halt borrowing at current high rates.

"Our new budget is the first balanced budget in Turkey for the past 50 years...Borrowing at high rates will stop. This is a revolution," Erbakan was quoted by the semi-official Anatolian news agency as saying.
Addressing a crowd in the northeastern town of Merzifon, Erbakan said the budget would speed up investment and bring no additional tax and price hikes.
Turkey's 6,255 trillion lira 1997 budget draft targets zero deficit, but independent analysts are sceptical such an ambitious goal is attainable.
The cash-short Turkish treasury has been offering high real returns of up to 40 percent to borrow from domestic markets since the early 1990s.

Interest payments on foreign and domestic debt have the highest stake in the 1997 budget spending with 29.8 percent, followed by personnel expenditures with a share of 26.8 percent. Investments have only 8.4 percent share.
Turkey's 1996 budget is expected to yield a deficit of around 1,300 trillion lira, up from the official target of 861 trillion lira.
